There the narration will also appear showing how Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) crossed the Tigris River during the Battle of Qaadisiyyah. The narration cites the announcement Hadhrat Hujr bin Adi (RA) made when he said, "What prevents you from crossing over these few droplets viz. the Tigris." He then recited the following verse of the Qur'aan;

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوْتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللّٰهِ كِتٰبًا مُّؤَجَّلًا
blocks.text: A person shall die only by the command of Allaah; (at a time that is) recorded (in the Lowhul Mahfoodh), fixed (and therefore can neither be postponed nor delayed). {Surah Aal Imraan, verse 145}
He then plunged his horse into the river and the other Muslims followed. When the enemy saw them, they took to their heels shouting, "Demons! Demons!"
Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) Drives a Fire Away

Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports a narration that mentions a fire emerging from Harra (a rocky terrain near Madinah). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then came to Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) saying, "Go and see to that fire!" "Who am I and what am I?" Hadhrat Tameem (RA) said. Hadhrat Umar (RA) however insisted until Hadhrat Tameem (RA) went with him. The narrator reports that he followed them as they proceeded to the fire where Hadhrat Tameem (RA) rounded up the fire with his bare hands until it returned into the crevice it had come out from, with Hadhrat Tameem (RA) behind it. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then remarked, "The one who has witnessed this can never be like the one who has not (because it serves to boost one's Imaan)."[^1] Bayhaqi and Baghawi have also reported a similar narration, as will be quoted in the chapter discussing unseen assistance from Allaah.
What Rasulullaah ﷺ saw when He struck A Boulder During Preparations for the Battle of Khandaq and the Glad Tidings he gave the Sahabah (RA)

A Sahabi (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the command for the trench to be dug, a large boulder presented an obstacle to the digging. Rasulullaah ﷺ took up a spade, placed his shawl beside the trench and recited:

blocks.arabic_text: وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَّعَدْلًا لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمٰتِهٖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيْعُ الْعَلِيْمُ
blocks.text: The words of your Rabb have been completed (perfected) in truth and justice. There is none to alter His words and He is the All Hearing, the All Knowing. {Surah An'aam, verse 115}
